art-057.label: Art. 57
art-057.text:
Art. 57. A pena de multa, graduada de acordo com a gravidade da infração, a vantagem auferida e a condição econômica do fornecedor, será aplicada mediante procedimento administrativo, revertendo para o Fundo de que trata a Lei nº 7.347, de 24 de julho de 1985, os valores cabíveis à União, ou para os Fundos estaduais ou municipais de proteção ao consumidor nos demais casos.
§ 1º A multa será em montante não inferior a duzentas e não superior a três milhões de vezes o valor da Unidade Fiscal de Referência (Ufir), ou índice equivalente que venha a substituí-lo.
§ 2º Quando as condutas previstas no art. 39, caput, incisos II e X, forem praticadas por importadores, produtores, distribuidoras, transportadores-revendedores-retalhistas ou revendedores varejistas de combustíveis, biocombustíveis ou derivados de petróleo, em qualquer etapa da cadeia de comercialização, a multa será de R$ 20.000,00 (vinte mil reais) a R$ 500.000.000,00 (quinhentos milhões de reais), hipótese em que não se aplica o limite previsto no § 1º.

decisions: Acts of this part (Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei nº 3.689, de 3 de outubro de 1941), Código de Defesa do Consumidor (Lei nº 8.078, de 11 de setembro de 1990)): each paragraph's life span is read from Planalto's annotated page of the act (del3689.htm, l8078.htm): struck wordings stay in place before the wording that replaced them, each closed by the source's own note ('Redação dada pela…', 'Incluído pela…', 'Revogado pela…'); text with no note is the act as enacted.
Credits come only from those notes; a changed article with no note naming a law stays uncredited.

A struck wording with no 'Revogado' note ends when the next wording of the same dispositivo (same label in the same article) starts; a Medida Provisória's wording with no later wording ends on the in-force day of the law that converted the MP (read from the MP page's 'Convertida na Lei' line).
Medidas Provisórias are dated by publication (CF art. 62: force of law from publication); laws by their own vigência clause, else LINDB art. 1 (publication + 45 days).

Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei nº 3.689, de 3 de outubro de 1941): in force 1942-01-01 (Decreto-Lei 3.689/1941 art. 810: 'Este Código entrará em vigor no dia 1º de janeiro de 1942' (published in the DOU of 13.10.1941, rectified 24.10.1941)).

Código de Defesa do Consumidor (Lei nº 8.078, de 11 de setembro de 1990): in force 1991-03-11 (Lei 8.078/1990 art. 118: 'Este código entrará em vigor dentro de cento e oitenta dias a contar de sua publicação' (published in the DOU of 12.9.1990, edição extra): 12.9.1990 + 180 days = 11.3.1991).

Headings (Parte, Título, Capítulo, Seção) and the marginal headings (rubricas) are kept in one file per act, titulos.md, one line each; a note standing alone after a heading is given to the heading lines just before it.

Text normalised once: NBSP to space, runs of spaces collapsed, curly quotes and dashes made plain, 'Art. 1o' written 'Art. 1º'; Planalto's link words ('Vigência', 'Produção de efeitos') and 'Vide' notes are dropped.
The consolidated pages print a revoked dispositivo as its bare label ('Art. 757.'); the check ignores those label-only lines, and the history leaves revoked text out.

Código de Processo Penal: the page's alignment is unreliable (heading name lines are often not centred), so headings are only Livro/Título/Capítulo/Seção lines, the name line right after one, and lines in capitals without a comma (as for the Código Penal).

Rules for struck text with no note of its own, each in the source's layout: 'run-revoked' - an earlier line of a struck run closed by one 'Revogado pela' note; 'heads' - a struck rubrica or heading falls with the struck dispositivo after it; 'heading-reworded' - a struck heading block followed, after struck articles, by the same heading reworded (CPP Capítulo V 'DAS PERGUNTAS AO OFENDIDO' -> 'DO OFENDIDO', Lei 11.690/2008) ends when the new block's note starts it; a struck '(VETADO)' line directly above wording a law's promulgated vetoed parts introduced stands from that law's day to the promulgation; the successor of a struck wording may lie past a heading reworded between the two wordings.

Typesetting slips read as unstruck: a struck ordinal sign or full stop inside unstruck text ('§ 1<strike>º</strike>', CDC art. 8; CPP arts. 312 and 313) and a struck cross-reference link (CPP art. 336: '(art. 110 do Código Penal)'); a strike that ends inside the last word of a struck wording (CPP art. 725 III: '... como tam</strike>bem ao juiz') is read as struck. A run of full stops left at the end of a line by removed notes becomes one full stop. 'Il - no concurso' (CPP art. 78) is read as the label 'II -'; 'Parágrafo Único' as 'Parágrafo único' (the text keeps the source's spelling).

Unstruck '(Revogado)' placeholders of the annotated page ('Parágrafo único. (Revogado).') stay in the text as Planalto prints them; the check ignores placeholder lines on both pages, since the consolidated page prints a placeholder ('IV - (revogado).', 'Art. 556. a Art. 560') where the annotated page keeps the struck wording.

Text before its law (coordinator rule): every line is dated by the in-force day of the law in its own note, so no wording appears before the law that made it; the parser checks this for every line with a 'Redação dada', 'Incluído' or 'Renumerado' note (see the count below). Court rulings Planalto shows only as 'Vide ADI ...' notes (the Lei 13.964/2019 juiz das garantias articles, ADI 6.298, 6.299, 6.300 and 6.305, among others) change no words on the page, so the history has no commit for them.

Código de Processo Penal, one difference from the consolidated page kept as it is: the annotated page strikes the heading 'CAPÍTULO II / DO JULGAMENTO' (Livro III, Título III) together with the arts. 556 to 562 under it, revoked by Lei 8.658/1993; the consolidated page still prints the heading with no article under it. The history follows the annotated page and ends the heading with the articles (27.5.1993).

Lei 11.689/2008 art. 1 re-enacted Livro II, Título I, Capítulo II (the Júri procedure, arts. 406 to 497: 'O Capítulo II do Título I do Livro II do Decreto-Lei nº 3.689 ... passa a vigorar com a seguinte redação'). Planalto prints the old chapter (with its amendments up to 2008) as one struck block, then the new chapter. Every struck line of the old block that no note or later wording ends is ended on Lei 11.689's in-force day, and every line of the new chapter without a note of its own starts that day, credited to Lei 11.689.

Lei nº 13.964, de 2019: the parts of Lei 13.964/2019 vetoed on 24.12.2019 were promulgated after Congress overrode the veto (CF art. 66 § 5; DOU 30.4.2021, printed at the end of the Lei 13.964 page): for the CPP, art. 3º-B § 1º and art. 14-A §§ 3º to 5º.

CDC art. 39 XI: Planalto prints, in place of the inciso, the editorial line 'Dispositivo incluído pela MPV nº 1.890-67, de 22.10.1999, transformado em inciso XIII, quando da conversão na Lei nº 9.870, de 23.11.1999' (the consolidated page too). It is kept as the source's text, starting on Lei 9.870/1999's in-force day and credited to it (the anachronism rule: not before the laws it names); the MP's own wording of XI is not on the page, so the history has no XI before then.

STF, ADI 2.797 (Plenário, 15.9.2005): declared Lei 10.628/2002, which added §§ 1º and 2º to CPP art. 84, unconstitutional; decision published in the DJ and DOU on 26.9.2005 (ata nº 25, STF case record), the day the version takes effect. Embargos de declaração (17.5.2012) fixed the effects from 15.9.2005; the history keeps the publication day. Planalto strikes both paragraphs, noting the case.
